title: Finite type descends in a ring tower through a faithfully flat finitely presented source algebra
statement: Let $R,A,B$ be commutative rings and let $R\to A\to B$ be ring homomorphisms, with $R\to B$ their composite. Suppose that $B$ is of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Then $A$ is of finite type over $R$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on any of the rings.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-fppf-integer-model] to the given faithfully flat finitely presented map $f:A\to B$. Obtain $C,D$, $u:C\to A$, $g:D\to B$ and $e:A\otimes_C D\simeq B$, with $e(a\otimes d)=f(a)g(d)$. In particular $C$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$ and $C\to D$ is faithfully flat. These are exactly the hypotheses required by that model lemma; the finite type hypothesis on $R\to B$ is not used yet.

source.place: Tag 0367, lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra, first sentence, using the absolute case of Algebra 034Y.

proof.text: Put $T=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$. The tensor-product universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $T\to A$, $r\otimes c\mapsto r_Au(c)$, where $r_A$ is the image of $r$ in $A$. A finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] supplies finitely many ring generators $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ of $C$. Every $t\in T$ is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; writing its $C$-coefficients as integer polynomials in the $c_i$ shows that $t$ is an $R$-polynomial in $1\otimes c_i$. Thus $T$ is finite type over $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. This is the elementary base-extension part of the general-base reduction in 034Y.

source.place: Tag 0367, first sentence; Algebra 034Y, final paragraph, base extension from Z to R, needing only finite type of the model base.

proof.text: Choose $R$-algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $e^{-1}(b_j)=\sum_{k=1}^{m_j}a_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}$, absorbing module coefficients into the $A$-factors. Introduce one variable $X_{jk}$ for each of these finitely many coefficients and put $P=T[X_{jk}]$. Let $\varphi:P\to A$ extend $T\to A$ and send $X_{jk}$ to $a_{jk}$. The images of $1\otimes c_i$ together with all $X_{jk}$ generate $P$ over $R$: expand the coefficients of each polynomial using the generators of $T$. Consequently $P$ is finite type over $R$ without a Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 0367, sentence beginning Since R to B is of finite type: explicit finite coefficient enlargement.

proof.text: Form $Q=P\otimes_C D$, where $C\to P$ factors through $T$. Since $C\to D$ is faithfully flat, [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] gives that $P\to Q$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, is faithfully flat. The tensor-product universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $q:Q\to B$, $p\otimes d\mapsto f(\varphi(p))g(d)$. Its image contains the image of $R$ and each $b_j=q(\sum_kX_{jk}\otimes d_{jk})$. Since these $b_j$ generate $B$ as an $R$-algebra, writing any element as an $R$-polynomial in them proves that $q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0367, coefficient enlargement and the assertion that the model map to B is surjective.

proof.text: The base change of $\varphi:P\to A$ along $P\to Q$ identifies with $q$. Explicitly $\theta:A\otimes_P Q\to B$ sends $a\otimes(p\otimes d)$ to $e(a\varphi(p)\otimes d)$. Its inverse sends $e(a\otimes d)$ to $a\otimes(1\otimes d)$. Both maps are well defined by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]; the balancing relation $a\varphi(p)\otimes z=a\otimes pz$ shows their composites fix every pure tensor, hence every element by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Moreover $\theta(1\otimes z)=q(z)$. Thus the complex $P\to A\to0$ becomes exact after tensoring with the faithfully flat $P$-module $Q$, since its first map is the surjection $q$ under this identification. By the exactness-reflection definition in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $P\to A\to0$ is exact. Its kernel at $A$ is all of $A$, so $\varphi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0367, displayed tensor comparison and faithful-flat reflection of surjectivity; exactness reflection is Algebra Definition 00HB.

proof.text: Let $p_1,\ldots,p_N$ be the finite $R$-algebra generators of $P$ obtained in step 3. Given $a\in A$, choose $p\in P$ with $\varphi(p)=a$. Express $p$ as an $R$-polynomial in the $p_i$ and apply $\varphi$. This expresses $a$ as the same polynomial in $\varphi(p_i)$. Hence these finitely many images generate $A$ over $R$, which is the conclusion by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 0367, final sentence: a surjective image of the finite type R-algebra P is finite type.
